housing: Gosport is a compact peninsula town between Portsmouth Harbour and the Solent, with a long naval history. The older streets in Forton, Elson and the town centre are Victorian and Edwardian terraces, while Bridgemary and Rowner have large post-war estates, some of them built for naval families and since regenerated. Lee-on-the-Solent has many bungalows and seafront flats, and former naval sites at Royal Clarence Yard and Haslar have been converted into apartments. Private renting is mostly terraced houses and flats.
checkinTips: Seafront flats in Lee-on-the-Solent: look for salt corrosion on window frames, balcony rails and door furniture, and photograph any damp on exposed walls.
Victorian terraces in Forton and the town centre: check for damp at the base of walls and in rear kitchens, and photograph yards and rear access.
Converted naval buildings at Royal Clarence Yard and Haslar: note fob and key counts, communal areas, parking and the condition of large period windows.
Post-war estate homes in Bridgemary: record the boiler, windows and doors, and the state of gardens and fencing.
Low-lying homes near the harbour and Solent shore: look for signs of past flooding or tidal damp in ground-floor rooms.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Gosport Borough Council's environmental health (private sector housing) team, after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
